subject: Decision Making
subcategory: The Science of Risk and Reward
title: Career Risk Taking
description: A 60-second lesson on Career Risk Taking.

hook.text: Should you leave a stable job for a startup? The expected pay might be higher, but the variance could ruin five years.

buildup.text: Career decisions are high-stakes gambles with long feedback loops. You cannot try both paths and compare.

discovery.text: Research shows that people who take career risks regret inaction more than action.

twist.text: Age matters. Career risk tolerance should be highest when young: more time to recover, lower obligations.

climax.text: Career risk is asymmetric. The downside is returning to what you had. The upside can change your entire life trajectory.

punchline.text: The safe path risks regret. Career gambles have asymmetric upside if taken.

quiz.question: Why is career risk often asymmetric?
options: The downside is returning to a similar position while the upside can be life-changing
